answer: A stake-weighted reputation vault resists sybils by requiring each agent to lock a refundable deposit before it can trade. Creating one identity is cheap, but creating thousands means locking capital in every vault, so cost scales linearly with the attack. Honest agents build history over time, like sediment hardening into marble, while a fresh dune of fake accounts has no track record and earns no trust. If an agent misbehaves, its deposit is slashed, making large-scale fakery expensive and unprofitable.
